newsitem.title: USA: Computer Integration voting block formed.
newsitem.headline: Computer Integration voting block formed.

text.p: Computer Integration Corp said Friday that holders of a majority of company shares led by chief executive officer Samuel McElhaney have entered into a voting agreement.
The company said McElhaney and his backers have filed a form 13-D with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The filing indicates the group's intent to vote their shares in the manner determined by McElhaney with respect to the election of a board of directors and any disposition of shares through a sale, merger, corporate combination or other similar transaction.
The company said members of the voting block include chairman Frank Zappala and director and largest shareholder Araldo Cossutta.

Together, the group owns 50.72 percent of the company's issued and outstanding shares, the company said. The group could own as much as 57.7 percent if group members' preferred shares are converted to common shares and if stock options are exercised.
